newsitem.title: USA: BASKETBALL-WNBA'S LIBERTY SET ATTENDANCE RECORD IN HOME OPENER.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-WNBA'S LIBERTY SET ATTENDANCE RECORD IN HOME OPENER.

text.p: The New York Liberty of the fledgling WNBA set what team officials said was a single-game attendance record for women's professional basketball in America when 17,780 attended their home opener at Madison Square Garden Sunday.
"It's the greatest feeling in the world," said flashy point guard Theresa Weatherspoon, a U.S. Olympic gold medalist and veteran of international pro basketball. "We're the record girls."

The crowd, with a much heavier flavoring of young girls than usually seen at the Garden, greeted the Liberty with frenzied cheering before the game began. Club officials wound up not closing off portions of the arena as originally planned.

"I'm used to crazy fans but not 17,000 of them," said Rebecca Lobo, whose perfect-season national collegiate championship with Connecticut and gold medal at the Atlanta Olympics helped popularise the sport in the United States.
"We had 30,000 fans at the Olympics but I don't know if they were as loud."

The Liberty remained the WNBA's only undefeated team at 4-0 -- and Lobo ran her personal undefeated streak to 101, counting two pre-season games -- by defeating the Phoenix Mercury 65-57 in a game that saw long stretches of doldrums marked by turnovers and poor shooting, especially in the first half.
Lobo said the team had only about a week and a half of real practice together.
"It will get better. You have to understand, some of us haven't played in a long time," said Weatherspoon, referring to the layoff since last summer's Olympics.
"We have a lot of things we have to work on but the chemistry is there."
